html:
Mansaf is the national dish of Jordan: lamb cooked in a sauce of jameed, dried fermented yoghurt, and served on a great platter of rice over thin bread, topped with almonds and pine nuts.

It comes from the Bedouin and village feasts of the land east of the Jordan, and Kerak is famous for it. Older versions used bulgur wheat, and rice became usual in the 20th century. It is eaten with the right hand from the shared plate, standing, at weddings, funerals and to welcome guests.

It stands for hospitality and the tribal roots of Jordan. UNESCO listed it in 2022. Compare couscous in the Maghreb.
sum: Mansaf is the national dish of Jordan: lamb cooked in a sauce of jameed, dried fermented yoghurt, and served on a great platter of rice over thin bread, topped with almonds and pine nuts.
